title: ImagePipeline Job Spec
description: The universal, provider-agnostic contract for one media-generation job. This is the public API: the same JobSpec drives the CLI today and an HTTP endpoint later. 'Any person's image + prompt' = a JobSpec with reference=<their upload> and spec.prompt_template=<theirs>. As of job-v2 the same contract also carries motion (media_type: video), either compiled deterministically by Remotion or generated — see the motion object.

allOf.description: An image job — media_type absent or 'image' — requires spec + engine exactly as job-v1 did. This is the conditional that keeps every existing v1 job valid while letting a Remotion job, which has no prompt and no generative backend, omit both.
A generative video is the image contract with a duration: it still names a prompt and a backend.
A Remotion render is fully described by its composition and its props; the remotion object is where that lives.

schema_version.description: Contract version. job-v1 is still accepted verbatim: v2 only ADDS the optional media_type discriminator and the motion/remotion objects, so every v1 job on disk validates unchanged. Bump only on breaking changes — this was not one.

media_type.description: The discriminator, and it DEFAULTS: absent means image. That default is the whole back-compat mechanism — a v1 job file is a v2 image job with the field elided, not a job that needs migrating.

motion.description: Required when media_type == 'video'. Engine policy (docs/census/2026-08-17-motion-engine.md §2): Remotion is canonical for deterministic UI/product motion — 77% of the reference's distinct pieces — because it renders the string it is given and re-renders per breakpoint for the cost of the compute. 'generative' is for atmospheric backdrops only, where nothing is verifiable so non-determinism is harmless.

engine.description: Which of the two paths. Authoritative per job, not per tenant.

duration_frames.description: Authoritative for Remotion; derived from the model's duration for generative.

width.description: A per-breakpoint cut is a SECOND job with the same composition_id and different dimensions — the desktop/mobile pattern the reference uses on every tab video.

loop.description: Flags the atmospheric case. No catalogued generative model advertises seamless looping, so a true value on a generative job means a loop-point pass is still owed.

remotion.description: Required when motion.engine == 'remotion'. Everything a deterministic render needs and nothing it does not: no network fetch, no clock, no font URL.

entry.description: Path to the registered root, e.g. 'motion/src/index.ts'.

props.description: The compiled props — INCLUDING the token subset, so a palette change alters the props, alters job_hash, and invalidates the cached render. That is the mechanism, not a convention.

props_provenance.description: Carries provenance into the media artefact, so a string rendered on a frame traces back to a declared field. 'default' is not a permitted source: sourced or empty, never invented.

font_files.description: LOCAL paths. A font referenced by URL is a network dependency and breaks portable determinism — the property that licenses using job_hash as a cache key at all.

id.description: Slug identifying this job; used in output filenames.

subject.description: Freeform key/value map. Each key is available as a {placeholder} in spec.prompt_template.

spec.description: The FEEDER: the CAD/engineering description + prompt that defines WHAT to render.

prompt_template.description: Prompt with {placeholder} tokens filled from subject + selected output fields ({composition}, {background}).

cad.description: Optional CAD/engineering spec: an inline string OR a path (resolved relative to the job file) to a .md/.txt extraction. Informational; fold into prompt_template as you see fit.

reference.description: The DESIRED TARGET image(s) the engine should match (look anchor). Null/absent for pure text-to-image. String path/URL, object form, or array of either for multi-anchor jobs.

optional.description: If true, a missing reference is a warning not an error.

output.description: The OUTPUT REQUIREMENT — varies case to case. Scalar params map to engine flags; composition/background are folded into the prompt.

imgtype.description: Label used in output filenames (e.g. card, hero, section).

aspect_ratio.description: e.g. 1:1, 4:3, 16:9. Passed to engine when supported.

resolution.description: e.g. 1k, 2k. Passed to engine when supported.

background.description: Freeform background requirement, folded into the prompt (e.g. 'near-black #0b0b0d, floating').

composition.description: Freeform composition requirement, folded into the prompt (e.g. 'upright 3/4 beauty shot').

engine.description: Which generative backend + model. Adapter-selected by name.

params.description: Escape hatch: extra '--name value' flags passed verbatim to the engine.
